flows.description: DF31: Summary lookups for permission checks.
DF02: Board/summary queries via ci-portal backend proxy.
DF03: Excel export requests via ci-portal backend proxy.
DF04: Full task operations via ci-portal backend proxy.
DF05: Gate operations via ci-portal backend proxy.
DF01: Webhook data query via ci-portal backend proxy.
DF55: PR event processing with account token.
DF06: M2M API calls to gateway.
DF08: Machine API full task trigger (ci-portal path).
DF09: Machine API gate calls (ci-portal path).
DF52: Config fetch and service discovery.
DF53: Executor registration and task dispatch.
DF11: Rule-set recompute and full task invoke callbacks.
DF37: Task queues, Redisson locks, AK/SK cache.

threats.title: Nacos configuration spoofing injects attacker-controlled credentials and endpoints
threats.description: An attacker able to publish config (or poison discovery) can inject attacker-controlled credentials and endpoints, steering the application to hostile services via Nacos config loading of security.part1 and all datastore credentials.
threats.mitigation: Restrict Nacos write/read access to trusted operators; use Nacos ACL/namespace isolation; validate config source integrity; separate discovery from sensitive config.

identity_key.attack_surface: Nacos config loading (DF52) for security.part1 and datastore credentials

threats.title: AES key and ciphertext co-located in the same Nacos namespace
threats.description: The AES key security.part1 and the encrypted secrets it protects are stored in the same Nacos namespace and config group (OPENLIBING), so one config compromise reveals both key and ciphertexts.
threats.mitigation: Move the key to a dedicated secrets manager with independent access control and rotation; avoid co-locating key and ciphertext in the same config artifact.

identity_key.attack_surface: Nacos config group OPENLIBING holding security.part1 key and ciphertexts (DF52)

threats.title: No code-level authentication on /apig/v1/** endpoints
threats.description: All four /apig/v1/** endpoints rely entirely on the Huawei APIG gateway for auth, so a gateway misconfiguration, weak AppCode, or bypass exposes unauthenticated task-trigger and status-read APIs.
threats.mitigation: Enforce a second in-code auth barrier (HMAC/API-key/signature validation) on /apig/v1/**; do not single-source auth to the gateway.

identity_key.attack_surface: /apig/v1/** M2M endpoints (DF07)

threats.title: Full request bodies logged at INFO on /apig/v1/** endpoints
threats.description: logger.info on every endpoint logs full request params including repoUrl, task params, and caller-supplied fields, landing sensitive data in log pipelines.
threats.mitigation: Redact or truncate request payloads before logging; log only non-sensitive identifiers (taskId, uuid); review log retention/access.

identity_key.attack_surface: INFO request logging on /apig/v1/** endpoints (DF06/DF07)

threats.title: Arbitrary scan task submission without quota or ownership checks
threats.description: Any authenticated (gateway-authorized) machine caller can submit arbitrary full/inc scan tasks for arbitrary repo URLs without quota or ownership checks, consuming Huawei CodeCheck scan quota and compute cost.
threats.mitigation: Add per-caller rate/quota limits and repo-ownership validation in code; bind machine callers to registered projects.

identity_key.attack_surface: M2M task-trigger endpoints /apig/v1/** (DF06/DF07)

threats.title: Unauthenticated MongoDB read access via webhook endpoint
threats.description: Any in-cluster caller can query 17 whitelisted collections (TASK_INC, TASK_RESULT_DETAILS, STATIC_ALARM_ISSUE, etc.) because the endpoint performs no authentication, so task/defect/alarm data is readable without permission.
threats.mitigation: Add an authentication/authorization barrier for this endpoint; scope queryable collections per-caller; audit reads.

identity_key.attack_surface: Webhook MongoDB query endpoint /ci-portal/webhook/codecheck/v1/find/by/mongoDB (DF01/DF20)

threats.title: NoSQL injection via webhook whitelist gaps on insert paths
threats.description: WebhookInputValidator blocks non-whitelisted table/field names on the readMongoDB path, but insertData validates only tableName and leaves nested queryData/mongoData unvalidated, so injection surface persists on future reachable paths.
threats.mitigation: Extend validateFieldName/validateValue to all write/insert paths; unit-test validator against operator objects and array types.

identity_key.attack_surface: Webhook insertData path to MongoDB (DF20)

threats.title: Unauthenticated internal endpoints allow unauthorized task triggers
threats.description: /internal/** relies on service-to-service trust with no credential, so any in-cluster pod can invoke pre-commit, rule-set recompute, and full task invoke endpoints.
threats.mitigation: Enforce mutual authentication (mTLS/API token) for /internal/**; verify caller identity (service account) before acting; restrict to the actual sibling services.

identity_key.attack_surface: /internal/** endpoints (DF11/DF54)

threats.title: Option injection into the auto-fix process via branch name
threats.description: CommandArgSanitizer.sanitizeBranchName allows a leading '-' and '..' sequences, so a branch like '--flag' is accepted and passed as an option value to auto-fix.sh -b, enabling option/argument injection into the shell script.
threats.mitigation: Reject branch names starting with '-'; strengthen sanitizeBranchName regex; pass branch via environment or stdin rather than argv.

identity_key.attack_surface: /internal/pre-commit auto-fix.sh option injection (DF11)

threats.title: Decrypted repo access tokens passed as process command-line arguments
threats.description: PipelineDelegateImpl.preMergeAndFix runs auto-fix.sh with decrypted tokens as argv, so the tokens are visible in the host process list (ps//proc) to any local observer.
threats.mitigation: Pass tokens via environment variables or a temp file with 0600 permissions; use ProcessBuilder with env; avoid argv for secrets.

identity_key.attack_surface: auto-fix.sh process argv with decrypted tokens (DF11)

threats.title: Unauthenticated result ingestion lets any in-cluster service spoof the CICD source
threats.description: POST /codescan/v1/result/receive (and /internal/codescan/v1/result/receive) accepts scan results from any caller, enabling injection of forged scan-run records and triggering SARIF parsing.
threats.mitigation: Authenticate the CICD caller (mTLS/service token); verify pipeline context integrity; audit ingestion.

identity_key.attack_surface: /codescan/v1/result/receive result ingestion (DF12)

threats.title: Unvalidated obsUrl enables SSRF and malicious-content parsing
threats.description: The DTO field obsUrl has only @NotEmpty with no scheme/host/domain whitelist, and arbitrary URLs are persisted and later fetched server-side by SarifParseServiceImpl, enabling SSRF and malicious-content parsing.
threats.mitigation: Validate obsUrl against an allowed OBS host/scheme allowlist; reject private/internal IP ranges and redirects.

identity_key.attack_surface: obsUrl field on /codescan/v1/result/receive (DF12)

threats.title: Full DTO logged at INFO including obsUrl, repoUrl, and pipeline context
threats.description: Static alarm receive logs the full DTO at INFO, sending sensitive pipeline and repository data into log pipelines.
threats.mitigation: Log only scanRecordId and non-sensitive identifiers; redact URLs.

identity_key.attack_surface: INFO DTO logging on result receive (DF12)

threats.title: Arbitrary obsUrl + resource consumption via unbounded parse events
threats.description: An in-cluster caller can submit unbounded parse events that cause repeated outbound OBS downloads and parsing work with no per-source quota/rate limit.
threats.mitigation: Rate-limit ingestion per source; cap concurrent parse work; validate URL before enqueue.

identity_key.attack_surface: Unbounded parse event ingestion (DF12/DF15)

threats.title: No authentication/authorization on full-task trigger
threats.description: POST /ci-portal/webhook/codecheck/full/task performs only a repoUrl blank-check with no format whitelisting, so any in-cluster caller can trigger full scans for arbitrary repo URLs.
threats.mitigation: Enforce caller authentication and repo-ownership validation; apply repoUrl format whitelisting on this path too.

identity_key.attack_surface: /ci-portal/webhook/codecheck/full/task (DF08/DF27)

threats.title: Full request params logged at INFO including repoUrl
threats.description: startFullTask logs the full params at INFO including repoUrl and project/branch, landing sensitive repository identifiers in logs.
threats.mitigation: Log only taskId after creation; redact request payloads.

identity_key.attack_surface: INFO request param logging on full task trigger (DF08)

threats.title: Gate status exposed by capability value (uuid) without authentication
threats.description: POST /ci-portal/webhook/codecheck/v1/task/status returns gate results for any uuid with no authentication; the uuid acts as a bearer credential, so a leaked/guessed uuid exposes and can manipulate gate outcomes.
threats.mitigation: Bind status queries to authenticated callers; require an additional auth factor; rotate/shorten token exposure.

identity_key.attack_surface: /ci-portal/webhook/codecheck/v1/task/status by uuid (DF09/DF28)

threats.title: Unencoded concatenation of client-supplied values into URLs
threats.description: InternalCodeIncDelegateImpl.handleFinishedTask builds openlibingDomain + '/apps/entryCheckDashCode/' + taskId + '/' + uuid with unencoded taskId/uuid, allowing parameter injection into the returned result URL.
threats.mitigation: URL-encode path/query components; validate taskId/uuid format before concatenation.

identity_key.attack_surface: handleFinishedTask result URL concatenation (DF09)

threats.title: Malformed pr_url triggers exception churn
threats.description: pr_url.split('/') requires >=5 segments but indexes up to prStrings[6], throwing ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException for 5-6 segment URLs and causing repeated error handling and 500s.
threats.mitigation: Validate PR-URL segment count and format up front; return 4xx for malformed input.

identity_key.attack_surface: pr_url parsing in InternalCodeIncDelegateImpl (DF09)

threats.title: Missing permission checks on 6 of 8 export endpoints
threats.description: Only /rule/set and /rule/set/export call AuthUtils.checkPermission; /download/log and summary/rule export endpoints expose task logs and rule data to any in-cluster caller without authorization.
threats.mitigation: Add permission checks to all export endpoints, especially /download/log; apply a consistent authorization filter.

identity_key.attack_surface: /ci-portal/excel/v1/** export endpoints (DF03/DF24)

threats.title: Client-supplied identity (userId) enables user impersonation
threats.description: userId is a @RequestParam on permission-checked export endpoints, so any caller can impersonate another user by passing their userId to satisfy AuthUtils.checkPermission.
threats.mitigation: Derive the user identity from an authenticated session/token, never from a client-supplied parameter.

identity_key.attack_surface: userId @RequestParam on export endpoints (DF03)

threats.title: Unvalidated filename concatenation enables header/response injection
threats.description: tableName + '.xlsx', fileName + '.log', projectName + '规则集.xlsx' build Content-Disposition filenames from unvalidated request parameters, enabling header/response injection and misleading filenames.
threats.mitigation: Sanitize/whitelist filename components; use Content-Disposition with safe encoding; validate tableName/fileName format.

identity_key.attack_surface: Content-Disposition filename building (DF03)

threats.title: Client-supplied identity on bulk shield-all operation
threats.description: POST /codecheck/inc/task/shield-all-result performs bulk defect shielding with userId taken from the request; the delegate's isReviewer check compares against the spoofable client value, allowing unauthorized shielding.
threats.mitigation: Derive userId from an authenticated session; require server-side reviewer identity; audit shield operations.

identity_key.attack_surface: /codecheck/inc/task/shield-all-result with spoofable userId (DF02)

threats.title: Unauthenticated summary/detail reads on board endpoints
threats.description: The 13 query endpoints under /ci-portal/v1/** have no controller-level auth, so board summaries, defect details, task file contents, and full/inc metrics are readable by any in-cluster caller.
threats.mitigation: Add consistent authorization for all read endpoints; enforce repo-level permission checks.

identity_key.attack_surface: /ci-portal/v1/** read endpoints (DF02/DF21)

threats.title: NoSQL query injection via unvalidated query models
threats.description: QueryDetailModel, QueryTaskFileContentModel, and IgnoredExtendDTO lack @Valid and whitelisting, so query criteria fields flow into MongoDB queries unsanitized.
threats.mitigation: Add @Valid + field whitelisting to all query DTOs; centralize NoSQL query construction.

identity_key.attack_surface: Unvalidated query DTOs into MongoDB (DF21)

threats.title: Over-broad authorization bypasses in AuthUtils.checkPermission
threats.description: checkPermission returns true unconditionally for roles admin/platform_operator regardless of project and for any menu with identification general_config, and assertAuthFromSummary returns true for any public repo, widening the authorization surface beyond least privilege.
threats.mitigation: Restrict admin bypasses to explicit project scopes; validate general_config handling; tighten public-repo assumptions.

identity_key.attack_surface: AuthUtils.checkPermission role/menu bypass logic (DF30)

threats.title: Permission decisions consume client-supplied userId
threats.description: AuthUtils permission decisions consume client-supplied userId from FileDownLoadController and CheckboardController rather than a server-authenticated identity, so horizontal privilege escalation is trivial by spoofing another user's id.
threats.mitigation: Replace client-supplied userId with session/token-derived identity at all checkPermission call sites.

identity_key.attack_surface: checkPermission call sites consuming client-supplied userId (DF30)

threats.title: Credential material (AK/SK ciphertext) in Redis queues and error logs
threats.description: syncRule() serializes {region, akSkVo} ciphertext AK/SK into a Redis task queue, and error paths log the map/JSON containing the AkSkVo ciphertext.
threats.mitigation: Do not persist AK/SK (even ciphertext) in task queues; redact credential fields from log messages; cache decrypted credentials in-memory with TTL instead.

identity_key.attack_surface: Redis queue rule_set:languages_severity_rule_set_task_queue and error logs (DF37)

threats.title: Rule-set sync dequeue/consume phase runs outside the Redisson lock
threats.description: For getAllAccountRule/syncRule/getProjectRuleSets only queue initialization is locked; if the lock is not acquired, consumers still process stale queue content, enabling duplicate or inconsistent rule-set sync.
threats.mitigation: Move the consume phase inside the lock or use idempotent consumption keys; clear queues on lock failure.

identity_key.attack_surface: Unlocked dequeue/consume of rule-set sync queues (DF37)

threats.title: HTML injection in full-task notification emails
threats.description: executionDurationJudgment builds an HTML email body by concatenating repoName, gitUrl, branch, and triggerTime without escaping, so attacker-influenced task metadata can inject HTML/phishing content into recipients' mail clients.
threats.mitigation: HTML-escape all interpolated fields; use a templating engine; send text/plain or sanitized HTML.

identity_key.attack_surface: Full-task notification email HTML body (DF42)

threats.title: Unsanitized persisted defect data enables stored injection
threats.description: Huawei CodeCheck API responses are written to MongoDB with only status/emptiness checks and no field-level sanitization of filePath/defectContent, allowing stored XSS/injection content to flow into downstream board rendering and exports.
threats.mitigation: Sanitize/normalize persisted defect fields; escape at render time.

identity_key.attack_surface: Unsanitized defect filePath/defectContent persisted to MongoDB (DF40)

threats.title: HTML injection in gate-notification emails
threats.description: sendExceedThresholdEmail and executionDurationJudgment interpolate taskIncEntity.getId(), mrUrl, triggerTime, projectName into unsanitized HTML bodies, so attacker-influenced MR data can inject HTML/phishing content.
threats.mitigation: HTML-escape interpolated fields; use a templating engine.

identity_key.attack_surface: Gate-notification email HTML body (DF48)

threats.title: Token-based repo operations on spoofable task data
threats.description: Decrypted account tokens drive git platform operations for task-supplied git URLs; tampered task records could redirect token use or trigger unwanted platform calls.
threats.mitigation: Validate git URL against registered repos before using tokens; bind token use to authenticated task origins.

identity_key.attack_surface: Token-based git platform operations keyed on task gitUrl (DF45/DF46/DF47)

threats.title: Raw dead-letter content logged by consumer
threats.description: handleDeadLetterEvent logs the raw dead-letter message; if task records or sensitive payloads enter the dead-letter queue, their content lands in logs.
threats.mitigation: Truncate/sanitize dead-letter payloads before logging.

identity_key.attack_surface: Dead-letter event logging (DF16)

threats.title: Unbounded SARIF download causes memory exhaustion
threats.description: SarifParseServiceImpl downloads the persisted obsUrl via openStream() with no content-length cap, byte limit, or connect/read timeout, so a malicious or oversized URL causes memory exhaustion in the Jackson parse.
threats.mitigation: Enforce max download size and timeouts; stream with a bounded reader; validate URL against an allowlist before download.

identity_key.attack_surface: Unbounded SARIF download triggered by parse event (DF17)

threats.title: No duplicate-parse protection on static-alarm consumer
threats.description: The consumer runs with concurrency 1-3 and takes no Redisson lock; duplicate parse events cause repeated OBS downloads, re-parses, and repeated MongoDB upserts, inflating cost and state churn.
threats.mitigation: Add idempotency/lock keyed on scanRunId; skip already-parsed runs.

identity_key.attack_surface: Duplicate parse events without idempotency (DF17)

threats.title: Message-trusted identity for bulk state changes
threats.description: ShieldAllMessage carries userId/op/type/scope published from client-supplied values, so a forged-userId message within the broker causes unauthorized bulk shielding and notification spam.
threats.mitigation: Re-validate the operator identity and permission at consume time; bind messages to authenticated callers; verify count/scope against source data.

identity_key.attack_surface: ShieldAllMessage userId/op trusted from broker message (DF18)

threats.title: HTML injection in shield notification email
threats.description: sendEmail builds an HTML body by concatenating detailUrl without escaping, enabling HTML injection into recipient mail clients.
threats.mitigation: HTML-escape detailUrl and all interpolated fields.

identity_key.attack_surface: Shield notification email detailUrl HTML body (DF18)

threats.title: Stored query-DTO tampering alters export scope
threats.description: StaticAlarmServiceImpl.processExport deserializes the stored export query StaticAlarmQueryDTO from the framework obs_file record and exports matching defects; tampering with the stored DTO changes which defect data is exported to files.
threats.mitigation: Verify the export query/scope against the requesting user's permissions before export; authenticate the export record origin.

identity_key.attack_surface: Stored StaticAlarmQueryDTO export scope (DF35)

threats.title: SSRF via server-side URL fetch of obsUrl
threats.description: downloadAndParse executes URI.create(obsUrl).toURL().openStream() with no scheme/host allowlist, redirect policy, or timeout; an in-cluster caller can make the service fetch arbitrary internal endpoints (metadata, internal services) and parse the response.
threats.mitigation: Validate obsUrl against an allowed OBS domain allowlist; block private/internal IP ranges and redirects; add connect/read timeouts.

identity_key.attack_surface: Server-side obsUrl fetch in downloadAndParse (DF49)

threats.title: Unbounded download/parse of oversized SARIF
threats.description: There is no content-length or byte cap on the SARIF InputStream fed to Jackson and no result/message size bounds in CodeQlSarifParser, so oversized SARIF causes memory exhaustion.
threats.mitigation: Enforce max download size, max parse elements, and timeouts; stream with a bounded reader.

identity_key.attack_surface: Unbounded SARIF InputStream fed to Jackson parser (DF49)

threats.title: Missing object-key validation in OBS bucket operations
threats.description: uploadFile/deleteObject/getObject pass the caller-supplied objectKey straight to the OBS SDK with no key-format or scope validation, so any caller with service access could address any object in the single configured bucket (defense-in-depth).
threats.mitigation: Enforce an object-key namespace/pattern allowlist; scope operations to the export prefix.

identity_key.attack_surface: OBS object-key passed unvalidated to SDK (DF51)

threats.title: MongoDB TLS hostname verification disabled
threats.description: MongoConfig enables SSL but sets builder.invalidHostNameAllowed(true), so the client does not verify the MongoDB server hostname, enabling MITM/eavesdropping on the MongoDB connection within the cluster (CWE-295).
threats.mitigation: Set invalidHostNameAllowed(false); pin the MongoDB server certificate/CA; enforce hostname verification.

identity_key.attack_surface: MongoConfig SSL hostname verification (DF20-DF50)

threats.title: Single shared MongoDB account with no least privilege
threats.description: The application uses one decrypted MongoDB credential for all collections and operations, so any application compromise or DB account leak grants full read/write over all scan/defect/alarm data with no per-collection or per-role separation.
threats.mitigation: Use separate MongoDB roles/users per function; enable MongoDB RBAC; scope credentials to least privilege.

identity_key.attack_surface: Single shared MongoDB credential (DF20-DF50)

threats.title: MySQL transport encryption depends on config-center JDBC URL
threats.description: DataSourceConfig decrypts the password but configures no TLS in code; if the JDBC URL does not enforce useSSL/requireSSL, MySQL traffic (including roles/permissions queries) travels plaintext in the cluster.
threats.mitigation: Enforce TLS/SSL in the JDBC URL (useSSL=true&requireSSL=true); verify via config and connection.

identity_key.attack_surface: JDBC URL TLS enforcement (DF30/DF38)

threats.title: Credential ciphertext at rest in Redis queues
threats.description: RuleSetScheduleTask persists {region, akSkVo} ciphertext AK/SK in a Redis list and task status markers; a Redis compromise exposes encrypted credential material and task data despite TLS.
threats.mitigation: Avoid persisting credential material in Redis; if needed, use short TTLs and encrypt at a separate layer; restrict Redis access via ACL/network policy.

identity_key.attack_surface: Redis queue rule_set:languages_severity_rule_set_task_queue (DF37)

threats.title: Plaintext AMQP messaging outside the prod profile
threats.description: RabbitConnectionFactoryConfig enables SSL only when the prod profile is active; beta/gama/icsl profiles inherit port 5672 and connect without TLS, so task/alarm messages travel in cleartext across the cluster.
threats.mitigation: Enable AMQPS (TLS) for all non-local profiles; enforce TLS via config; consider message signing for integrity.

identity_key.attack_surface: Non-prod RabbitMQ connections on port 5672 (DF13-DF19)

threats.title: Scan results delivered without integrity verification
threats.description: The CICD service posts scan results to /codescan/v1/result/receive over plain service-to-service HTTP with no signature or mutual auth, so tampered scan results (altered SARIF/obsUrl) would be accepted and parsed as authoritative.
threats.mitigation: Add message signature/HMAC or mTLS between CICD and codecheck; verify pipeline context integrity.

identity_key.attack_surface: Unsigned scan result delivery to /codescan/v1/result/receive (DF12)

threats.title: No mutual authentication on Feign calls to framework service
threats.description: openlibingFrameworkClient calls are HTTPS but not mutually authenticated; an in-cluster actor could impersonate the framework service and return forged export-task state, altering the CAS export workflow.
threats.mitigation: Enable mTLS/service-account identity verification for Feign calls.

identity_key.attack_surface: Feign call to openlibing-framework without mTLS (DF36)

threats.title: Internal callbacks to /internal/** are unauthenticated
threats.description: openlibing-coderepo calls /internal/** (rule-set recompute, full task invoke) with no credential, so the trust relationship can be impersonated by any in-cluster actor to trigger recompute/full-scan work.
threats.mitigation: Authenticate sibling-service callbacks (mTLS/service token); verify caller identity in /internal/**.

identity_key.attack_surface: Unauthenticated /internal/** callbacks from coderepo (DF11)

threats.title: Weak or absent XXL-Job executor accessToken
threats.description: xxl.job.admin.accessToken is injected from config; if the token is empty or weak, an in-cluster actor can register a spoofed executor or dispatch forged jobs to the application.
threats.mitigation: Enforce a strong, rotated accessToken for executor registration; restrict xxl-job admin network access.

identity_key.attack_surface: XXL-Job executor registration accessToken (DF53)

threats.title: Nacos key/ciphertext co-location defeats encryption at rest
threats.description: The AES key security.part1 and every encrypted secret reside in the same Nacos group/namespace (OPENLIBING); one Nacos read compromise yields both key and ciphertexts, defeating encryption at rest.
threats.mitigation: Store the key in a dedicated secrets manager with independent ACLs and rotation; split sensitive config from application config; enable Nacos ACL/encryption-at-rest.

identity_key.attack_surface: Nacos group OPENLIBING co-locating security.part1 and ciphertexts (DF10/DF52)

threats.title: OBS AK/SK dependency from config exposes all bucket artifacts
threats.description: Bucket access uses obs.access-key-id/obs.secret-access-key decrypted from config; a config/credential leak exposes all SARIF scan artifacts and export files in the single bucket.
threats.mitigation: Rotate OBS AK/SK; use STS short-lived credentials; restrict bucket ACL to the service account.

identity_key.attack_surface: OBS AK/SK from config-center credentials (DF49/DF51)

threats.title: Single point of auth on the /apig/v1/** boundary
threats.description: The entire /apig/v1/** boundary trusts the APIG gateway for authentication/rate limiting/audit; a gateway misconfiguration, AppCode leak, or bypass would expose unauthenticated M2M endpoints.
threats.mitigation: Add an in-code secondary auth barrier; monitor gateway config; restrict AppCode rotation.

identity_key.attack_surface: APIG gateway as sole auth for /apig/v1/** (DF06/DF07)

threats.title: AK/SK dependency and request-object logging to HuaweiCodeCheck
threats.description: Scan delegation, rule sync, and result polling use tenant AK/SK; error paths log the whole APIG Request object holding the decrypted key/secret, and an AK/SK leak grants control of scan creation, rule-set sync, and full result readback for all tenants.
threats.mitigation: Rotate AK/SK; enforce per-tenant scoping; avoid logging credential-bearing request objects.

identity_key.attack_surface: Tenant AK/SK signed requests and Request-object logging (DF27/DF29/DF39/DF41/DF44)

threats.title: Access tokens in GitCode API URL query parameters
threats.description: GitCodeHelper appends ?access_token=<decrypted token> to API URLs; tokens can leak via proxy/access logs, browser history, or Referer headers (CWE-598).
threats.mitigation: Send tokens via Authorization header instead of query params; ensure HTTP client does not log URLs.

identity_key.attack_surface: access_token in GitCode API URL query string (DF45/DF55)

threats.title: Access tokens in Gitee API URL query parameters
threats.description: GiteeHelper appends ?access_token=<decrypted token> to API URLs; tokens can leak via logs, browser history, or Referer (CWE-598).
threats.mitigation: Send tokens via Authorization header; avoid logging full URLs.

identity_key.attack_surface: access_token in Gitee API URL query string (DF46)

threats.title: Inconsistent GitHub token handling causes mis-credential usage
threats.description: GithubPlate.getAccessToken returns accountInfo.getGithubAccessToken() without SecurityHelper.decrypt and getAccountInfo never populates the github token, so GitHub flows may use an un-decrypted/empty token, masking the real auth state.
threats.mitigation: Align GitHub token decryption with other platforms; populate/persist github token consistently; fail closed on missing token.

identity_key.attack_surface: GitHub token decryption/population inconsistency (DF47)

threats.title: SMTP without TLS transmits password and email bodies in plaintext
threats.description: EmailUtil.sendEmail configures only mail.smtp.auth=true with no STARTTLS/TLS property, so the sender password and email bodies are transmitted to the mail server in plaintext.
threats.mitigation: Enable STARTTLS/TLS (mail.smtp.starttls.enable=true / mail.smtp.ssl.enable=true); enforce server certificate validation.

identity_key.attack_surface: EmailUtil SMTP transport without TLS (DF42/DF48)

findings.title: Missing code-level authentication on M2M /apig/v1/** endpoints

identity_key.attack_surface: /apig/v1/** M2M endpoints (HwApigController.java lines 69-141)

findings.title: Unauthenticated internal & machine endpoints allow unauthorized task triggers

identity_key.attack_surface: /internal/**, /ci-portal/webhook/codecheck/full/** and /ci-portal/webhook/codecheck/v1/** endpoints

findings.title: Missing authorization on portal/board/webhook read endpoints

identity_key.attack_surface: /ci-portal/excel/v1/**, /ci-portal/v1/** and webhook query endpoints

findings.title: Client-supplied identity enables authorization bypass

identity_key.attack_surface: client-supplied userId in FileDownLoadController lines 128/153, CheckboardController line 239, ShieldAllMessage

findings.title: SSRF via SARIF obsUrl server-side fetch

identity_key.attack_surface: SarifParseServiceImpl.downloadAndParse obsUrl fetch (line 160)

findings.title: NoSQL injection via insufficient input validation

identity_key.attack_surface: unvalidated QueryDetailModel/QueryTaskFileContentModel/IgnoredExtendDTO query criteria

findings.title: Sensitive data logged at INFO across controllers

identity_key.attack_surface: INFO request-body logging (HwApigController line 94, StaticAlarmReceiveServiceImpl line 52, CodeCheckEventConsumer lines 124-127)

findings.title: HTML injection in notification emails

identity_key.attack_surface: text/html email bodies built by concatenation (EmailUtil line 165, SaveFullTaskResult lines 294-299)
